findings.F1: Fees are not why the book fails: the 2332 trades are all long, with a mean gain before fees of 1.00% (t 4.23 over 2332 trades) against a mean fee of 0.10%, so the failure is the Calmar of 0.36 against a 0.75 bar, which comes from deep drawdowns (mean per-window maximum drawdown −14% to −22% by coin, a worst book day of −38%, and a 1% quantile of invested-day book returns of −13%).
findings.F2: The book's losses sit in falling-market years: trades entered in 2018 lost a mean −3.3% before fees (n 220, win rate 33%), in 2022 −2.1% (n 322, win rate 29%) and in 2019 −0.8% (n 277), while 2020 and 2021 earned +3.8% (n 374) and +5.4% (n 325); the active bars' non-overlapping 5-bar forward return was likewise −2.5% in 2018 (n 74) and −2.3% in 2022 (n 114), against +3.8% and +4.0% in 2020 and 2021.
findings.F3: Short holds lose and long holds pay: trades held 1.5 days or less made a mean −2.04% before fees (n 534), those held 1.5 to 3.5 days −1.29% (n 559), those held 3.5 to 7.5 days −0.17% (n 548), against +3.03% for 7.5 to 15.5 days (n 392) and +10.5% beyond 15.5 days (n 291); the 1101 trades held 3.5 days or less summed −1812% before fees, against +4147% for the 1231 longer ones, with an overall win rate of only 39%.
findings.F4: A larger forecast earns only weakly more: non-overlapping 5-bar forward returns were +1.12% when the forecast was above 2.5 (n 721, t 2.74) against +0.41% on flat bars (n 2522, t 1.85), with no ordering among the small middle buckets (n 29 to 69, means −1.7% to +2.4%); by entry forecast, trades entered above 5 made +1.00% (n 1919) and those entered between 2.5 and 5 made +1.34% (n 336).
findings.F5: Inside the active set, the size of the 20-day rise and the calm do not grade the gain: by 20-day-return tercile the 5-bar forward return was +0.39%, +2.04% and +0.76% (n about 255 each); by 20-day-volatility tercile it was +0.57% for the calmest third against +2.03% for the most volatile third.
findings.F6: Exits caused by volatility leaving the calm half are costly: invested days that ended on a bar where volatility had left the calm half averaged −0.11% (n 1003), against +0.24% on bars still calm (n 5045); such bars were 41% of the worst 2% of invested days (n 121), and those worst days summed −18.1 against a total of +11.1 over all invested days.

ideas.idea: A calm, positive 20-day rise in one coin is followed by further upward drift only while the coin's price also stands above its own long-term moving average; in a coin trading below that average, the same calm rise is followed by falling prices.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take the calm-uptrend long only when the coin is above its long-term average and refuse it when the coin is below.
ideas.name: long trend gates calm drift

ideas.idea: The upward drift after a calm rise belongs to coins whose 20-day return has stayed positive for several consecutive weeks; a coin whose 20-day return has only just turned positive gives back the rise within the next few days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would enter only once the positive 20-day return has persisted, and would refuse fresh turns that tend to end in quick losing exits.
ideas.name: persistent rise carries drift
